newsitem.title: USA: Ohio corn, soy harvest still behind average pace.
newsitem.headline: Ohio corn, soy harvest still behind average pace.

text.p: Corn and soybean harvests in Ohio made respectable progress during the week ended November 10, but both remain more than two weeks behind historical averages, according to the latest crop weather report from the state's agricultural statistics service.
Soybean harvest was complete on 86 percent of the acreage, 13 points above the previous week, but still two weeks behind the average pace of 99 percent.
Corn harvesting was 51 percent complete, up from 35 the previous week. That figure compared with the five-year average of 73 percent.
Farmers completed 95 percent of the intended winter wheat seedings, but weather may cause some intentions to be abandoned, the report said.
Wheat had emerged on 78 percent of the acreage, compared with 69 the previous week, 93 last year and the average of 89 percent.
Topsoil moisture was 32 percent surplus, 66 adequate and two percent very short. There were 4.5 days suitable for fieldwork during the week ended November 8.
